build: the 0.7.0 PGO release build: the binaries of the GitHub release assets nanocodec-0.7.0-x86_64-linux and -aarch64-linux (commit ce89975ea; tools/dev/pgo_build.sh: profile-guided, trained by encoding public clips with every shipped preset and decoding the streams; fat LTO, one codegen unit, x86-64-v3 code generation on x86); the decoders' SIMD kernels are chosen at run time (AVX-512 on Granite Rapids, NEON and SVE2 on Graviton 4)
browser_build: the v0.7.0 browser module (tools/web/build.sh, its relaxed-SIMD build: SIMD128 plus relaxed SIMD)
method: Each process reads its stream into memory, then decodes it 3 times, each pass with a fresh one-thread decoder and frames discarded; neither side is charged process start-up, probing, demuxing or output. 5 interleaved rounds (order reversed every other round): 15 passes per decoder and stream; the figure is the median pass.
harnesses: ours: nanocodec decode --bench; FFmpeg and dav1d: libavcodec-bench (tools/anchors/libavcodec_bench.c, packets demuxed by libavformat before timing); libvpx, VVdeC, AVM and dav2d: vpx-bench, vvdec-bench, avm-bench, dav2d-bench (tools/anchors/*_bench.c), each against its pinned static library, units split in memory before timing.
browser_method: tools/web/ffmpeg_wasm_yardstick.py under node (V8), one process per run, 7 interleaved rounds: ours the BrowserDecoder.decode calls (the display hand-off, I420 to RGBA, is not included), ffmpeg.wasm the sum of its decode_video calls as -benchmark_all logs them; neither is charged module start-up, probing or demuxing. The browser runs come from the first session on each machine (2026-11-27, before the PGO re-time); the native column beside them is the PGO build's, from the later session.
ffmpeg_wasm: @ffmpeg/core 0.12.10, the official single-thread build: FFmpeg 5.1.4 under emscripten with --disable-asm and -O3 -msimd128 (compiler-generated SIMD128 only, FFmpeg's hand-written SIMD kernels off); it has no AV1, VVC or AV2 decoder
streams: Two stream sets. Benchmark streams: 7 clips of the BP-4 "ours" held-out set (one per content class; 960x540 to 1280x720, 600 frames, the 1200 kbps rung), each coded by our six encoders at Medium and by x264 medium, x265 medium, libvpx VP9 rt 7, SVT-AV1 M10 and libaom rt 8 (the benchmark's streams). Earlier yardstick streams (2026-11-23): 720p to 4K, among them camera recordings (Axis, Hanwha, a Novatek bodycam) and streams from x264, x265, openh264, SVT-AV1, libaom and libvpx. Our streams come from development builds; only the decoders are 0.7.0's.
plain_build: Beside it, in the same rounds: the plain release build of the same commit (no PGO, as crates.io builds it), the page's secondary column
